datasets.title: Additional HealthLink hospital-directory locations
datasets.description: Nine source directory entries extend the existing reviewed registry; eight have independently reviewed building/campus points and one remains unlocated. These are newly released entries, not newly opened hospitals.
notes: Nine source directory entries extend the existing reviewed registry; eight have independently reviewed building/campus points and one remains unlocated. These are newly released entries, not newly opened hospitals.

A value of one means one reviewed directory entry. It is not beds, patient volume, staffing, service availability or an independent acute-care hospital. Named pavilions retain their building grain within larger campuses.

The 91 original service-location records include 82 records matched to 79 already-reviewed sites. Those matches are retained in coverage receipts and omitted from this additions view; St. Paul’s same-address building aliases are not counted as separate hospitals.

Source capture is 29 April 2026. Original province YT is preserved for Whitehorse despite the BC file name. Current representative OSM points, independently checked against operator addresses and campus plans, do not locate participants or individual clinical services.

Dr. Al Hogg’s directory point and returned named building differ spatially; the shared campus address is insufficient to establish a precise historical building match. Its source entry remains visible without a location code.

rows.site_grain: Named building on Peace Arch Hospital campus
rows.location_note: The HealthLink directory point and returned named OSM building centroid differ by about 180 metres. The operator confirms the shared campus address, but the precise building and historical directory match remain unresolved. No point is assigned.

rows.location_note: Operator campus plan and published clinical-location address confirm 2775 Laurel Street. Returned named OSM building at that address supplies the representative point. Outpatient building presence does not establish beds or service capacity.

rows.site_grain: Named building on Vancouver General Hospital campus
rows.location_note: Operator campus plan confirms Willow Pavilion at 805 West 12th Avenue; the named OSM building provides a representative centre point. The map does not identify individual wards, entrances, service availability or an independent hospital.

rows.site_grain: Named building on UBC Hospital campus
rows.location_note: Operator campus plan distinguishes Detwiller at 2255 Wesbrook Mall from Koerner and Purdy. Returned named OSM building gives the representative centre point. The original directory point is near another part of the campus and is not reused for this separate building.

rows.site_grain: Named building on UBC Hospital campus
rows.location_note: Operator campus plan distinguishes Purdy at 2221 Wesbrook Mall from Koerner and Detwiller. Returned named OSM building gives the representative centre point. Source directory coordinates are not treated as a shared building point or artificially separated.

rows.site_grain: Hospital campus, represented at the main hospital building
rows.location_note: Yukon government and operator confirm 5 Hospital Road. OSM returns two named buildings on the same hospital campus; one representative main-building point is used, not two hospitals. Original source province YT is retained despite the BC filename. This is a directory location, not a service-area allocation.

Health authority location page and Providence operator publications confirm 7801 Argyle Street in Vancouver. Returned named OSM node at that address provides a representative location. This is the Vancouver site, not same-named hospitals elsewhere.

datasets.title: Northern Health reported capital projects
datasets.description: 64 distinct printed project rows: 30 in the 2020–2022 report and 34 in the 2022–2024 report. Each record retains its source page, table and row; repeated generic names are not deduplicated into one project.
notes: 64 distinct printed project rows: 30 in the 2020–2022 report and 34 in the 2022–2024 report. Each record retains its source page, table and row; repeated generic names are not deduplicated into one project.

Published project values describe the report’s listed investments, not annual spending, delivered capacity, clinical outcomes or an NHHR benefit. Values are nominal Canadian dollars; report periods are preserved literally.

Project value and regional health district funding are distinct source columns. A dash remains null, not zero. Funding codes, including the published SNRHD label for Fort St. John, are retained as printed rather than corrected from geography.

The 46-row dedicated extract omits 18 printed projects and truncates headings and wrapped descriptions. The complete 64-row generic table is reconciled to the original Northern Health PDF pages and repaired through explicit reviewed row bindings.

Current facility points and separately labelled address-parcel references provide reporting context only.
